'''Peter Putnam''' (May 20, 1927–December 7, 1987) was an American [[physics|physicist]] and [[philosophy|philosopher]]. He worked on topics related to the [[observer effect (physics)|observer effect]] and [[theory of mind]], but never published his work.

== Life ==
Putnam was born in 1927, the son of wealthy parents John and Mildred Putnam. He studied physics at [[Princeton University]] as both an undergraduate and Ph.D., apprenticing during the latter with [[Albert Einstein]], and studying with [[John Archibald Wheeler|John Wheeler]]. He also served in the [[U. S. Navy]] for three years.
<ref name="bhs">{{cite web |title=Peter Putnam - Killed by a Drunk Driver |url=https://bratenahlhistorical.org/index.php/peter-putnam/ |website=Tragic Happenings |publisher=Bratenahl Historical Society |access-date=17 December 2025}}</ref>

Despite his familial wealth, Putnam worked as a [[janitor]], donating his inheritance to charity, including funding the [[Putnam Collection of Sculpture, Princeton University]] and [[The Nature Conservancy]]. He died at the age of 60 after being hit by a drunk driver in [[Houma, Louisiana]]. His notebooks are kept at the library of the [[American Philosophical Society]] in [[Philadelphia]].<ref name="nautilus">{{cite news |last1=Gefter |first1=Amanda |title=Finding Peter Putnam |url=https://nautil.us/finding-peter-putnam-1218035/ |access-date=17 December 2025 |work=Nautilus |date=17 June 2025}}</ref>
